# Corpus files whose trees differ from tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-tcl's
# (the grammar mep loaded from nixpkgs before), reviewed, where this
# grammar is right and the old one wrong. Tcl's own parser accepts every
# corpus file, so the oracle cannot tell; see README.md. Generated by
# classifying the first difference in every top-level command the old
# grammar read without errors; each file lists every reason it needed.
# Format: <path glob>  # why.  Read by tools/ts_grammar_diff (grammar-diff).
#
# Reasons:
#   ns: old ends a `$a::b` or `::a::b` name at the `::`
#   split: old splits one word in two at a character Tcl keeps inside a word (`:`, `"`, `(`, `)`, `${...}`, `\ `)
#   hash: old reads a lone `#` line as a word; it is a comment
#   exprlex: old lexes expression operands such as `3-int` or `2,` as one word
#   unpack: old takes `{*}` followed by a space for expansion; it is a braced word
#   contcomment: old ends a comment at a backslash-newline, which continues it
#   bare: old leaves a one-word command (`return`, `::tcltest::cleanupTests`) as a bare word outside any command
#   data: braced text that is not a script (an unbalanced quote or bracket, a stray `]`); old read commands into it
#   ternary: `?:` is right-associative
#   dollar: a `$` not followed by a name is literal
#   unbraced: an unbraced expression of more than one word, or a command with too few words for its shape, is an ordinary command
#   bool: `while true`: the unbraced bare word is labelled a number
